messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kernel exception (CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS) observed on gpu-decode-node-34 during streaming path — error-rate spike +50% at 13:02 UTC
maya (oncall): seeing the page, joining now. any customer-facing impact?
alex (infra): yes, node-34 showing repeated CUDA exceptions, container restarts 3x in 7m. stack trace points to decode kernel during nvcc op.
sam (sre): tagged node-34 as unhealthy, moving traffic off via router-weight 0. doing rolling drains on the rack.
maya (oncall): good. can we quick-mitigate at the model level? maybe throttle streaming or enforce max_tokens cap?
jordan (eng-ml): we can set a runtime header override to enforce max_tokens=256 for the affected model variant (open-l2-decoder-v1). that should reduce KV growth and avoid the kernel path triggered by long sequences.
alex (infra): pushing temporary rule now: `redwoodctl routing set-weight node-34 0 --ephemeral` and `redwoodctl model update-config open-l2-decoder-v1 --header-overrides 'max_tokens=256' --ephemeral`
ops-bot: Executing: redwoodctl routing set-weight node-34 0 --ephemeral
ops-bot: OK — weight set to 0 (will auto-revert in 2h if not confirmed)
ops-bot: Executing: redwoodctl model update-config open-l2-decoder-v1 --header-overrides 'max_tokens=256' --ephemeral
ops-bot: OK — ephemeral config applied to model open-l2-decoder-v1 in region-us-west
jordan (eng-ml): applied. also enabling conservative batching for that model: batch_size_max=8 to avoid large kernels.
sam (sre): node drain in progress, 8/10 connections migrated, no more restarts observed in the last 90s.
maya (oncall): any request drops recorded during the spike? need CS triage for impacted customers.
emily (cs): we have 3 customer tickets reporting truncated streaming responses in the 13:00-13:05 window (Account IDs: acct-842, acct-19, acct-77). I'll prepare a status blurb — want me to mention temporary throttling + ongoing investigation?
jordan (eng-ml): yes please mention we applied a temporary max_tokens cap and lowered batch size. that should be the mitigation while we investigate root cause on kernel side.
alex (infra): capturing logs for node-34 and kernel-livelogs:```
[13:02:10] cuda: illegal address at decode_kernel.cu:231
[13:02:11] containerd: restarting container redwood-decode-34 (exit code 137)
[13:03:05] nvml: GPU 0 ECC errors: 0
[13:03:06] runtime: freed 2.1GB KV-cache, mem usage down to 42%
```
sam (sre): I also saw a pattern: the failing requests had user-supplied max_tokens > 2000 and large prompt prefixes; that triggers long-kernel attention windows. need to add a guard on the request path to clamp abusive max_tokens while we fix the kernel bug.
maya (oncall): agreed. jordan, can you add a hotfix to clamp header on the router (reject or clamp >1024 to 1024) for a short window?
jordan (eng-ml): deploying clamp at the router layer now: `routerctl set-policy clamp_max_tokens=1024 for model=open-l2-decoder-v1`
ops-bot: Executing: routerctl set-policy clamp_max_tokens=1024 for model=open-l2-decoder-v1
ops-bot: OK — clamp active in region-us-west (propagation ~30s)
alex (infra): after router clamp + model header override, no further container restarts for 10m. fatal kernel calls stopped.
emily (cs): posting update to the three customers: brief explanation + mitigation applied. tag them for follow-up when root cause is known.
maya (oncall): starting an incident document (INC-2026-045) with timeline + actions. sam, alex, jordan please add diagnostic artifacts to the doc.
sam (sre): added coredump + kernel logs under INC-2026-045/artifacts. created JIRA: INFRA-1428 to track kernel-side reproduction.
jordan (eng-ml): will run smaller reproducer on a dev node with debug kernels and ASAN flags. expect initial hypothesis by EOD.
emily (cs): sending initial CS update now. low-to-medium impact, 3 customers affected, mitigation applied.
maya (oncall): I'm handing this off to sam for the overnight watch. next oncall @alex will monitor the node rotation progress. I'll post a follow-up in 30m with status. :white_check_mark:
